questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university had a good reputation, there were student-friendly facilities, and the university was located in an English-speaking country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It would have been a 10/10 experience if not for the pandemic and the industrial strike that took place during my stay.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was alright. There was a lot of information, which made it difficult to navigate.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I booked some appointments with the Visiting Students team. Also, I was connected with an Erasmus adviser in case I had any further queries.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The staff was ready to help immediately after arrival. However, it took a while (and quite a lot of correspondence with different people) before I found my contact persons.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not easy. After applying for 10+ accommodations, I was lucky to get one positive reply. My best tip is to keep on trying. Sometimes the private accommodations get available rooms close to the starting date because someone changed their mind. Also, I lived in City Center instead of West End (where the University is located), which I am glad I did, so I ended up knowing most of Glasgow pretty well.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Yes, it is expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is challenging to find housing, but not impossible.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Personally, the course registration went smooth because I got accepted into all my applied courses.

However, most of my fellow exchange students had a period where they were not enrolled in enough courses, which made the situation somewhat doubtful. Anyway, it was easier to change courses in the introduction weeks than expected.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I applied for courses before I went to Glasgow. In the introduction weeks, it was possible to change the courses (also after you have attended a few tutorials).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I was connected with an Enrollment adviser. Furthermore, it was possible to message the course convenors.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Fully successful. I also changed one of my courses during the stay.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I do not have any advice. The staff are so helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Note that there might be some additional courses which are allowed for exchange students to take but do not appear in their course catalogue. Personally, I could have chosen to take Labour Law, but I did not know that until it was too late.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was overall appropriate. I had three courses: one honours level and two undergraduate levels.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was very similar to the University of Copenhagen's style. The main difference was that all the tutorials were compulsive to attend, and they were more question-based and less group work-based. It was essential to prepare all the questions because the lectures could ask out of nowhere.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Roman Law Of Property & Obligations (LAW1007)
Foundations of Evidence Law (LAW2052)
Intellectual Property Law (Sem 2) (LAW3038)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend IP-law due to Brexit. We took a post-Brexit view in the course, which was interesting since the UK still uses EU law, but at the same time, tries to be independent and develop its own case law. Furthermore, I would recommend Evidence Law if others want to try a course concerning common law.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Membership in the sports organization of the University (GUSA) and membership in the Handball team

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing and food were more expensive than expected. However, transport and beers were less expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: At the beginning of the academic semester, there was a Sports Fayre and a Social Fayre, which was an excellent opportunity to meet all the clubs etc. and sign up for their events. Unfortunately, I did not know about the Sports Fayre before it was too late, so I just showed up for sessions without prior notice.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything. Also, activities I did not even know existed.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Anything. It is a great way to meet new people, think of something different and practise your English.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore Scotland in general. Also, the Northern part of England is quite beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, the Scottish culture is similar to the Danish.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join some of the activities at the University and chat with people in the classrooms (yes, we do not do that in Denmark, but it is pretty normal in Scotland).

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The public transport system is way different. You cannot count on it, timewise.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendly people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Remember to enjoy every minute and try as much as possible! 
2) It is always raining and windy. But sometimes it is in ridiculous circumstances that the funniest moments happen, so always remember a raincoat (so you do not get sick). Also, I would recommend hiking shoes if you are out of the city on an adventure.
3) Take to the fayres and chat with randoms

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are good public transport deals in Scotland, so spend an afternoon researching the possibilities. Furthermore, it is prevalent to have student discounts (compared to Denmark), so remember to ask in the shops, bars etc.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To be outside my comfort zone, improve my English and make friends for a lifetime.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The fact that you are on your own.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Undoubtful the best decision I ever made.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
